translations.text: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. That man was truthful, outstanding, righteous, and devoted to God, keeping away from every evil deed.
Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.

His livestock amounted to seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred pairs of oxen, and five hundred female donkeys. He had herdsmen, a large household staff, and extensive undertakings on the land. That man was wealthy among the people of the east.
His sons would go together and drink every day, bringing their three sisters along to eat and drink with them.

Whenever the days of drinking were over, Job would send for them and purify them. He would rise early and offer sacrifices for them according to their number, and a calf as a sin offering for their souls. For Job would say, “Perhaps my children have thought evil things against God in their hearts.” This was what Job did continually.
One day the angels of God came and stood before the Lord, and the devil came among them. He had been going around the earth and walking through it.
The Lord said to the devil, “Where have you come from?” The devil answered him, “I have explored the earth and walked about under heaven, and here I am.”
The Lord said to him, “Have you given thought in your heart to my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth: outstanding, truthful, and devoted to God, keeping away from every evil thing.”
The devil answered before the Lord, saying, “Does Job serve the Lord for nothing?
Have you not fenced in what is outside and inside his house, and all his possessions around him? You have blessed all his work and multiplied his livestock on the earth.
But stretch out your hand and touch everything he has, and see whether he will bless you to your face!”
Then the Lord said to the devil, “Look, I am putting everything he owns into your hands. But do not touch him.” And the devil went out from the Lord’s presence.
One day Job’s sons and daughters were drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house.
Just then a messenger came and said to Job, “The pairs of oxen were plowing, and the female donkeys were grazing beside them.
Raiders came and carried them off. I alone escaped and came to tell you.”
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, “Fire came from heaven and burned the sheep, consuming the shepherds as well. I alone escaped and came to tell you.”

While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, “The horsemen formed three divisions, surrounded the camels, and carried them off. They killed the servants with swords. I alone escaped and came to tell you.”
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking in their oldest brother’s house.
Suddenly a great wind came from the desert and struck the four corners of the house. The house fell on your children, and they died. I alone escaped and came to tell you.”
At this, Job rose, tore his clothes, and shaved the hair from his head. Then he fell to the ground and worshiped.

He said, “I came naked from my mother’s womb, and I will go away naked again. The Lord gave them, and the Lord took them away. What happened was what pleased the Lord. May the Lord’s name be blessed.” In all these things that came upon him, Job did not sin at all before the Lord, nor did he attribute foolishness to God.
One day the angels of God came and stood before the Lord, and the devil came among them.
The Lord said to the devil, “Where are you coming from?” The devil said before the Lord, “I have explored the earth and walked about everywhere, and here I am.”

The Lord said to him, “Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth: innocent, truthful, outstanding, and godly, keeping away from every evil thing. He still holds to his innocence, yet you called for his possessions to be destroyed for no reason.”
The devil answered the Lord, “Skin for skin! A man will give everything he has for his life.”
But no—stretch out your hand and touch his bones and his flesh, and see whether he will bless you to your face.
The Lord said to the devil, “Look, I am handing him over to you. Only spare his life.”
The devil went out from the Lord’s presence and struck Job with a terrible sore from his feet to his head.
He took a potsherd to scrape away his pus and sat on the dung heap outside the city.

After a long time had passed, his wife said to him, “How long will you endure, saying, ‘Look, I will wait a little longer, looking forward to the hope of my deliverance’? For your memory has vanished from the earth—your sons and daughters, the pains of my womb and the labors over which I struggled in vain amid hardships. You sit among foul worms, keeping watch in the open air, while I wander about as a servant, going from place to place and from house to house, waiting for the sun to set so that I may rest from the labors and hardships that now beset me. But say a word against the Lord and die.”

He looked into her face and said to her, “You have spoken like one of those foolish women. If we have received good things from the Lord’s hand, shall we not endure bad things?” In all these things that came upon Job, Job committed no sin with his lips before the Lord.

His three friends heard about all the troubles that had come upon him. Each came to him from his own country: Eliphaz, king of the Temanites; Bildad, ruler of the Shuhites; and Zophar, king of the [?]. They came to him together to comfort him and visit him.
They saw him from a distance but did not recognize him. They cried out loudly and wept. Each tore his robe, and they scattered dust on their heads.
They sat beside him for seven days and seven nights, and none of them spoke, for they saw that his suffering was severe and very great.
After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed his day,
saying:
“May the day on which I was born perish, and the night on which they said, ‘It is a boy!’
Let that night become dark. May the Lord above not seek it out, and may no light fall upon it.
“May darkness and the shadow of death seize it. May gloom come over it. May that day be cursed.
“And that night—may darkness seize it. May it not become a day of the year; may it not be counted among the days of the month.
“Instead, may that night become distress. May neither gladness nor joy come to it.
“May the one who curses that day curse it, the one who will subdue the great sea monster.
Let the stars of that night grow dark, and let them not endure or come into the light. Let it not see the dawn rising.
“For it did not shut the gates of my mother’s womb; it would have spared me these sufferings.
“Why did I not die in the womb? When I came out of the womb, why did I not perish immediately?
“Why were my knees raised [?]? Why did I suck at the breasts?
“I would have been forgotten and at rest,
“with the kings and counselors of the earth, who exalted themselves through their swords,
“or with rulers who have much gold, who filled their houses with silver,
“like a miscarriage coming out of its mother, or like those infants who never saw the light.
“There the wicked no longer feel the fury of their anger, and there those whose bodies are weary have rested.
“They are together forever, without hearing the tax collector’s voice.
“The small and the great are there, and the slave who fears his master.
“Why was light given to those in suffering, and life to the souls of those in distress,
“who desire death but have not found it, searching for it as for treasures?
“They rejoice when they find it.”
For death is a rest for a person, for God has shut him in.
For sighing came to me before my food, and I weep, living in fear.
For the fear I was anxious about came upon me, and what I fear overtook me.
I had no peace, I was not quiet, and I had no rest; instead, anger came upon me.
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
“Have you often been spoken to in distress? But who can bear the force of your words?
For if you have taught many and encouraged the hands of the weak,
you have raised up the sick with your words and strengthened the knees of the weak.
But now suffering has come upon you; it has touched you, and you have become troubled.
Isn’t your fear rooted in foolishness, and your hope in the wickedness of your way?
Remember: who has perished while holy? Or what righteous person has been uprooted and destroyed?
As I have seen, those who plow wrongdoing and sow it will reap hardships for themselves.
But they will fall at the Lord’s command, and they will perish through the spirit of wrath.
The strength of a lion, the voice of a lioness, and the pride of the dragons have been broken.
The ant-lion perished because it had no food, and the lion cubs were scattered from one another.
But if your words had contained a true statement, none of these evils would have overtaken you. Will my ear not hear marvelous things from him?
There was fear and a noise at night, while fear fell upon people.
Terror and trembling seized me and shook my bones violently.
A spirit came over my face, and the hair on my flesh bristled.
I stood up but saw nothing. I looked but found no form before me; instead, [?] dew, and they were hearing a voice.
For what can happen? Can a person be pure before the Lord? Or can a person be sinless in his deeds?
If he does not even trust his servants, and has found fault with his angels,
then what about those who live in these houses of clay? We too are made from this same clay, and something like a moth destroyed them.
They do not last from morning until evening, and they perished because they cannot help themselves.
For they were breathed upon and dried up, and they perished because they had no wisdom.
Call out and see whether anyone will listen to you, or whether you will see any holy angel.
For indeed anger destroys the fool, and jealousy kills the one who goes astray.
I saw foolish people putting down roots, but immediately they withered where they stood.
Their children are far from safety. They are beaten at the gates of those who are lower than they are, and there is no one to rescue them.
For righteous people will eat what these people gathered, but they themselves will not escape disaster, and their strength will wither.
For suffering does not come out of the earth, nor does trouble sprout on a mountain.
Rather, a person is born to suffer, while young vultures fly in the heights.
But as for me, I will plead with the Lord. I will cry out to the Lord, who is above everyone.
He is the one who made these great and unsearchable things, these glorious things and these wonders beyond counting.
He gives rain upon the earth and sends water beneath the sky.
He lifts up the lowly and raises up those who are perishing.
He overturns the plans of the intelligent, and their hands will accomplish nothing real.
He catches the wise in their own wisdom, and he has shattered the plans of the cunning.
Darkness will meet them during the day, and at noon they will grope about as though it were night.
They will perish in war, but a weak person will escape from the hand of someone stronger than he is.
The powerless will have hope, and the mouth of the oppressor will be shut.
Blessed is the person whom the Lord has corrected. Do not reject the Almighty’s instruction.
For he causes them pain and sets them on their feet again in their place. He wounds, and his hand heals again.
He will save you six times in your troubles, and on the seventh, evil will not touch you.
He will rescue you from death during famine, and in war he will save you from the power of iron.
He will hide you from the lash of the tongue, and you will not fear the evils that are coming.
You will laugh at oppressors and lawless people. You will not be afraid of wild beasts.
For wild beasts will obey you.
Then you will know that your household will obey you, and the dwelling place of your tent will not sin.
You will know that your descendants are numerous, and your children will be like all the grass of the field.
You will come to the grave like wheat in its [?], harvested in its season, or like a heap on a threshing floor, gathered in at its proper time.
Look, we have investigated these things in this way, and these are the things we have heard.
But you know in your heart what you have done. Then Job answered, saying:
“If only someone would measure my anger and weigh my sufferings together on a balance!
For they would indeed be heavier than the sand on the shores of the sea. But if my words are disgraceful,
For the Lord’s arrows are in my body, and their fury drinks up my blood. Whenever I speak, they pierce me.
For what happens? Does a wild donkey cry out over growing grass as it searches for its food? Does an ox cry out when there is food in its feeding trough?
Do people eat bread without salt? Or is there any flavor in empty words?
For my soul cannot be still, and I see that my food stinks like the smell of a lion.
If only he would grant it to me, and my request would come, and the Lord would give me what I hope for! The Lord has begun; let him wound me, but do not let him destroy me completely.
May my city become a tomb for me, the city on whose walls I used to leap. I will not hold back, for I have not lied about God’s holy words.
For what strength do I have to endure? Or how much time do I have for my soul to hold out?
Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh made of bronze?
Or have I not trusted in him? His help has gone far away from me.
Mercy has abandoned me, and the Almighty’s care has forgotten me.
I have become like a brook that has dried up, and they have passed me by like these waves.
Those who used to fear me have now risen against me like snow or frozen ice.
Just as it melts when heat comes, and no one knows the place where it was.
This is my situation too: everyone has abandoned me. I have perished and am outside my home.
I have seen the roads of the Temanites, the paths of the Sabeans.
Those who look will be put to shame, those who put their trust in these possessions and these cities.
But you too have risen against me—against me without mercy. Now that you have seen my wound, be afraid.
For what happens? Have I asked you for anything, or do I need your strength,
to save me from my enemies or to rescue me from the hand of oppressors?
Teach me, and I will be silent. Tell me where I have gone astray.
But the words of a truthful person are contemptible! For I did not ask you for strength.
And the rebuke in your words will not heal me, for I will not tolerate the [?] of your speech either.
Yet you rise against the orphan and pounce on your friend.
Now, then, let me look into your faces, so that I do not lie.
Sit down, and let no injustice occur; come together again for the truth.
For there is no injustice on my tongue. Does my palate not ponder wisdom?
Is not a person's life on earth a time of trial, and his life like that of a daily laborer?
Or like a slave who fears his master and has found shade? Or is it not like a hired worker waiting for his wages?
This is also my situation: I have endured empty months, and nights of suffering have been assigned to me.
When I lie down, I say, “When will morning come?” And again, when I get up, “When will evening come?” I am filled with suffering from evening until morning.
My body is rotting with foul worms. I break up clods of earth as I scrape away my pus.
My life is swifter than speech, and it has perished in empty hope.
Remember that my life is a breath, and my eye will not see good things again.
I have vanished like a cloud cleared away beneath the sky. When a person goes down to the underworld, he does not return to come back up.
He will not return to his own house, and his place will not recognize him again.
I too will not restrain my mouth. I will speak in my distress, while my soul is in anguish.
Am I the sea or the dragon, that you have set your attention on me and prepared evils against me?
I said, “My bed [?] will comfort me, and I will bring myself a word in private upon my bed.”
You frightened me with dreams and terrified me with visions.
You will separate my soul from my spirit and my bones from death.
For I will not live forever, so that I should be patient. Leave me alone, for my life is empty.
For what is a human being, that you have exalted him, or that you pay attention to him?
Or that you visit him in the morning?
Or that you judge him whenever he rests? How long will you refuse to leave me alone and give me no respite, even until I swallow my saliva in peace?
If I have sinned, what can I do to you, you who know people's hearts? Why has he set me against you? I am a burden to you.
Why have you not overlooked my wrongdoing and cleansed my sin? Now I will go into the earth, and I will not return to be sought.
Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
How long will you say these things? A spirit of many words is in your mouth.
Will the Lord act unjustly when he judges? Or will the one who created everything trouble the righteous?
If your children were the ones who sinned before him, he handed them over to the power of their lawlessness.
But you, plead with the Lord Almighty; plead with him.
If you are pure and truthful, he will hear your plea, and he will establish a righteous dwelling for you.
Your beginnings will be prepared, but your latter days will be beyond description.
Ask the earliest generation, and investigate the lineage of the ancestors.
For we were born yesterday and know nothing, for our lifetime on earth is a shadow.
Will they not teach you and tell you, and bring forth words from their hearts?
Does papyrus sprout on water, or does the reed grow tall on water?
Beneath its root [?], and it is not cut by any sickle; it does not dry up before it drinks.
This, then, is how everyone who forgets the Lord ends, for the hope of the godless is destruction.
For his house will be deserted, and his dwelling will become a spider’s web.
If he sets his house upright, it will not stand; if he holds on to it, it will not endure.
For it does not rot in the sun, and its flower comes out amid its decay.
It will lie on a heap of stones and live among pebbles.
If the place buries it, it will not deny it. Have you not seen anyone like this, nor been amazed at what I am saying?
For such is the downfall of the godless, and he will cause another to sprout from the earth.
For the Lord will not abandon the innocent, and he will not accept any gift from the godless.
But he will fill the mouths of the truthful with laughter and their lips with praise.
Your enemies will clothe themselves in [?], and the dwelling of the godless will cease to exist.
Then Job answered and said:
“Truly, I know that this is how things are established. For how can a human being be righteous before the Lord?
For if he wishes to go to court with him, he will not listen to him, so that he cannot answer him with even one word from his lips.
For he is wise in heart, strong and great. Who has resisted him and endured?
He moves the mountains without their knowing it; he overturns them in his anger.
He shakes the earth down to its foundations, and its pillars tremble.
He tells the sun, ‘Do not rise,’ and it does not rise, and he seals up the stars.
He alone made heaven, and he walks on the sea as someone walks on dry land.
He made the Pleiades, the evening star, Arcturus, and the chambers of the south.
He made these great, unsearchable and glorious things, and these wonders beyond number.
If he passes by me, I will not see him, and if he goes past me, I will not notice.
If he destroys them, who will bring them back to life? Or who will say to him, ‘What have you done?’
For anger does not turn him aside; the sea monsters beneath heaven have been bowed down by him.
If he listens to me, he will examine my words; I will plead for his judgment.
For even if I am righteous, he will not listen to me. If I call and he listens, I will not believe that he has listened to me.
Will you answer me in a storm? For he has multiplied my wounds for no reason.
He will not let me breathe, for he has filled me with my pains.
For he prevails over my strength. Who, then, can oppose his judgment?
For even if I am righteous, my mouth sins; and even if I am blameless, I come out crooked.
For if I have sinned, I do not know it in my heart; nevertheless, my life is taken away.
That is why I said that anger destroys the great and the powerful.
For the wicked will die an extraordinary death, but they laugh at the righteous.
For I have been handed over to the ungodly.
For my lifetime was swifter than a runner; they fled and did not see.
Is there a trace of the path of ships, or of an eagle flying in search of its food?
For if I say, “I will forget while speaking,” I will bow my head and sigh.
But I tremble in all my limbs, for I know that you will not leave me pure.
But since I am ungodly, why have I not died?
For even if I wash myself in snow and cleanse myself with pure hands,
You have thoroughly soaked me in filth; my robe has become foul.
For you are not a human being like me, so that I could take legal action against you and we could come to judgment together.
If only there were a mediator between us, listening and rebuking us both,
let him take his rod off me, and do not let the fear of him terrify me.
I would not be afraid, but I would speak, for I do not know myself to be like this.
Suffering in my soul, I will lay my words against him; sighing, I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
Let me say to the Lord, “Do not teach me to sin. And why are you judging me for these things?”
Is it good for you if I sin, since you have abandoned the works of your hands but paid attention to the counsel of the wicked?
Do you see as a human being sees?
Or is your lifetime a human lifetime, or are your years human years,
that you have searched for my lawlessness and investigated my sin?
For you know that I have not sinned, but who can escape your hands?
Your hands shaped me and made me; afterward, you turned and struck me.
Remember, then, that you shaped me from clay, and you will return me to the earth again.
Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh and wove me together with bones and sinews.
You placed life and mercy within me, and your care preserved my spirit.
Since you have these things in your heart, I know that you have power over everything, and nothing is impossible for you.
For if I sin, you will watch me, but you have not cleansed me of my lawlessness.
For woe to me if I sin! Even if I am righteous, I cannot lift up my head, for I am full of disgrace.
For they lay traps for me like lions that tear apart, and once again you turned and utterly destroyed me.
You examined me anew, treated me with great anger, and brought trials upon me.
Why did you bring me out of the womb? I should have died, and no eye would have seen me.
And I would have been like someone who does not exist. For why did I not die when I came out of the womb?
Is not the span of my life short? Leave me alone so that I may rest a little.

Before I go to the place from which I will not return, to a land of darkness and gloom, a land of everlasting darkness, a place where there is no light and where no one can see [?] among human beings.
Then Zophar the Minaean answered, saying:
“Anyone who speaks many words hears a reply to them. Or does a talkative person think he is righteous?
Blessed is the person whose life is short. Do not be excessive in your words, for there is no one bringing a case against you.
Do not say, ‘For I am pure in my deeds, and I am blameless in his sight.’
But how will the Lord speak with you?

Then he will tell you the power of wisdom, for it will be twice as great as your own. Then you will understand that what has come upon you from the Lord is what you deserve for the sins you have committed.
Will you find the Lord’s footsteps, or will you reach the limits of what the Almighty has made?
Heaven is high—what can you do? Do you know what is deeper than the realm of the dead?
Or what exceeds the measure of the earth, or the breadth of the sea?
If he brings them all up, who will say to him, ‘What have you done?’
For he himself knows the deeds of the lawless. Having seen their improper deeds, he will not overlook them.
But if a man swims with his hands, a man born of a woman is a wild donkey in the desert.
But if you had purified your heart, you would have raised your hands to him.
If there is any sin in your hands, let it be far from you. Do not let injustice remain in your dwelling.
For this is how your face will become pure, like filtered water. You will keep yourself free from defilement and will not be afraid.
And you will forget your troubles like a wave that has passed you by, and you will not be disturbed.
Your prayer will be like the morning star, and life will dawn for you at noon.
You will be confident because you have hope, and out of your anxieties and concerns, peace will appear to you.
For you will rest, and there will be no one to oppose you. Many will turn and plead with you.
But safety will depart and leave them, for their hope is destruction. The eyes of the ungodly will fail.
Then Job answered, saying:
“So, you are people! Will wisdom die with you?
I too have understanding, just like you.
For a righteous and choice man has become a laughingstock.
For he has been prepared for an appointed time to fall at the hands of others,
so that his houses may be plundered by the lawless. Nevertheless, let no wicked person think of escaping. Will those who provoke the Lord not also face examination?
But ask the animals and see if they will tell you; ask the birds of the sky and see if they will inform you.
But speak to the earth, to see whether it will answer you.
Is not the soul of every living thing in his hand, and the spirit of every human being?
For the heart tests words, and the palate tastes food.
Wisdom comes with a long time, and learning with a long life.
Wisdom and power are with him; counsel and understanding are his.
If he tears down, who will build? If he shuts people in, who can open for them?
If he holds back the water, he will make the earth dry; and if he releases it upon the earth, he will destroy it or lay it waste.
Power and strength are with him; learning and wisdom are his.
He is the one who sends counselors into captivity, and he has confounded the judges of the earth.
He is the one who seats kings on their thrones.
He is the one who sends priests into captivity, and he has overthrown the rulers of the earth.
He is the one who changes the lips of the faithful. He has understood the wisdom of the elders, and he has healed the humble.
He is the one who reveals the deep things of darkness, and he has understood the light of the shadows of those who go astray.
He who changes the hearts of the rulers of the earth led them astray on a path they do not know.
They will grope in darkness, not in light, and wander like drunken people.
Look, my eye has seen these things, and my ear has heard them.
I know what you know, and I am no more foolish than you.
No, I will speak with the Lord and argue my case before him, if he is willing.
But you are doctors who do wrong and healers of every evil.
If you keep silent, it will count as wisdom for you.
Listen to the argument from my mouth, and pay attention to the judgment of my lips.
Are you not speaking in the Lord’s presence and uttering a word before him?
Or can you hide? You yourselves pass judgment.
For it is good if he examines you, since, in doing all these things, you attach yourselves to him.
Then will he not rebuke you if you show partiality in secret?
Will his mighty acts not shake you? Terror from him will fall upon you.
Your boasting will become like ashes to you, and your body is of earth.
Be silent so that I may speak and find relief from my anger.
Let me fill my mouth with my flesh and put my life in my hands.
If the mighty one destroys me, since he has begun, I will still speak and argue before him.
And this will bring me salvation, for no deceit will enter his presence.
Listen, listen to my words, for I will speak while you listen.
Look, I am approaching judgment, and I know that I will be shown to be righteous.
For who will bring a case against me?
He will do two things for me.
Withdraw your hand from me, and do not let the fear of you terrify me.
You will call the one who will listen to you, or you will speak, and I will answer you.
How many are my sins and my lawless deeds? Show me what they are.
Why do you hide from me and set me against you?
Will you be afraid like a leaf shaken by the wind, or oppose me like grass carried away by the wind?
For you have written bitter things against me and laid upon me the sins of my youth.
You have put my foot in a stock, guarded all my actions, and reached down to the roots of my feet.
These wear out like wineskins or like a moth-eaten garment.
For a person born of a woman is short-lived and full of anger.
Or like something that has blossomed and withered, he flees like a shadow and will not remain.
Have you not taken account of such a person, and made him come before you for judgment?
For who can be clean from defilement? No one.
Even if his lifetime on earth is only one day, his months are counted by him. You have appointed a time for him, and he cannot go beyond it.
Withdraw from him so that he may rest and enjoy his life like a hired worker.
For there is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its sprouting will not cease.
For even if its root grows old in the earth and dies on a rock,
its trunk sprouts at the scent of water, and they will cut it like a new plant.
But when a person dies, he is gone; when a young man falls, he does not return.
But if the sea disappears for a time and the water drains away and dries up,
when a person lies down, he will not rise, nor will they awaken one another as long as heaven exists.
For it would have been good if you had kept me safe in the realm of the dead, hidden me until your anger ceased, and set a time for me when you would remember me.
For if a person dies, will he live? After he has completed the days of his life, I will wait until I come into being again.
You will call, and I will answer you. Do not abandon the works of your hands.
You have counted all my sins, and no lawlessness will escape you.
You have sealed up my sins in a bag and marked what I did that was beyond my control.
You have crushed him completely, and he has gone away. You looked at him with your face and humbled him.
When his children became numerous, he did not know; if they become fewer, he does not know.
But his flesh suffers pain, and his soul mourns.
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
Will a wise person answer with the wisdom of a spirit? For he died in anguish of the belly.
He rebukes with inappropriate words and with words that have no benefit in them.
You too have cast aside your fear of him and spoken words of this kind before the Lord.
You are bound by the words of your mouth, and you have felt no shame before the words of rulers.
Your mouth condemns you, not I, and your lips testify against you.
For what happens? Are you the first human being born, or were you brought forth before the hills?
Or have you heard the Lord’s decree? Has wisdom reached you?
For what do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that we do not understand?
You have been scourged only a little for your sins, yet you have spoken far beyond measure.
What has your heart dared to do, and what have your eyes looked upon?
For you have poured out anger before the Lord and uttered words of this kind from your mouth.
For what is a human being, that he should be pure, or one born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
If he does not put his trust in his holy ones, and heaven is not pure in his sight,
[?] is loathsome and unclean—the man who drinks injustice like water.
Listen to what I am telling you, and I will tell you what I have seen:
the things that the wise will tell, which their fathers did not hide from them [?].
No foreigner came among them.
The whole life of the ungodly person is spent in anxiety, and the years allotted to a ruler are numbered.
Fear is in his ears, and whenever he thinks, “I am secure,” then he will be utterly destroyed.
Let him not trust that he will escape the darkness, for they have already thrust him into the power of the sword.
They have made him food for vultures, and he knows within himself that he is destined for slaughter.
A day of darkness will terrify him; distress and affliction will seize him like a commander who has fallen before a soldier.
For he raised his hand against the Lord and stiffened his neck against the Lord Almighty.
He rushed at him with insolence.
He lives in deserted cities and will enter abandoned houses. Others will take the things that he prepared.
He will not become rich, nor will his possessions remain; he will not cast a shadow over the earth.
Nor will he escape the darkness. The wind dries up his shoots, and his flower falls off.
Let him not trust that he will endure, for what comes to him will be empty things.
His shoot will perish before its time, and his branches will give no shade.
They will harvest him like an unripe grape before his time, and he will fall like an olive blossom.
For death is the testimony of the ungodly, and fire will burn the houses of those who accept bribes.
He will conceive troubles within himself, and what comes from him will be empty. His heart will be pregnant with deceit.
Then Job answered, saying:
For I have heard many things like these. You are all comforters who bring trouble.
For what will happen? Is there an orderly arrangement to the words of the spirit?
I too could speak as you do. If your soul were in the place of mine, I would assail you with words; I would shake my head at you.
There would be strength in my mouth, and I would not hold back the movement of my lips.
For if I speak, I will not feel pain from my wound; and if I remain silent, I will have no more relief.
But now he has exhausted me, made me a fool, and seized me.
He has unleashed his anger and struck me down. He has ground his teeth against me and struck me with the arrows of his robbers.
He has attacked me with the glare of his eyes and struck me on my cheeks. They have rushed upon me all at once.
For the Lord has handed me over to the oppressor and thrown me to the ungodly.
He shattered me when I was secure. He seized my hair and tore me apart. He set me up as a target.
They surrounded me with spears, hurling them at my kidneys without mercy. They poured my gall onto the ground.
They struck me down with blow after blow. They rushed at me violently.
They dressed me in sackcloth, and my strength failed in the dust.
My heart has burned from weeping, and a shadow lies over my eyelids.
Yet there was no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
Earth, do not cover the blood of my flesh, and let there be no resting place for my cry.
Now look: my witness is in heaven, and the one who knows me is on high.
My plea reaches the Lord, and my eye sheds tears in his presence.
But a rebuke will come to a person before the Lord.
My allotted years have come, and I will go along the road from which I will not return.
I will perish, carried away by a spirit. I need someone to bury me, but I have not found him.
I plead as I suffer. Indeed, what have I done?
Strangers have stolen my possessions.
My eyes waste away over my children.
They have made me a byword among the nations, and I have become a laughingstock to them.
For my eyes have grown dim from my anger, and they have all surrounded me completely.
The truthful are astonished at this, and the righteous rise up against the sinner.
The faithful person will follow his path, and the holy person will gain strength through his hands.
But no—you are all contending, for I do not find truth among you.
My days have passed in turmoil, and the cords of my heart have snapped.
For if I endure, the underworld is my home, and they have spread my bed in darkness.
I have called death my father, and destruction my mother and sister.
Where, then, is my hope now? Or will I see good things?
Or will they go down with me to the underworld? Or will we go down to the earth together?
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said, “How long will you refuse to be silent?
Wait, so that we too may speak.
Why have we remained silent before you like these animals?
Anger has come upon you. What is to happen, then? If you die, will the earth become deserted, or will the mountains be torn down to their foundations?
The light of the ungodly will be extinguished, and their flame will not burn.
For his light will become darkness for him in his dwelling, and his lamp will be extinguished over him.
The least will lay snares for his possessions, and his plans will stumble.
His foot is caught in a trap, and he will be entangled in a net.
Snares will come upon him
all around him, and strong men will destroy him. Many will surround his feet while he is bewildered with hunger.
A slaughter of children has been prepared for him.
They will eat the tendons of his feet.
Death will devour his side, and safety will depart from his dwelling. Distress will seize him, together with a royal accusation.
His memory will perish from the earth.
They will bring him out of the light into darkness.
He will not be known among his people, nor will his household survive under heaven. Instead, others will live among his possessions.
Those who came later groaned over him, while those who came before were astonished.
These are the houses of the oppressors, and this is the place of those who do not know the Lord.
Then Job answered and said:
How long will you torment my soul and crush me with words?
Know very well that it is the Lord who has made me like this. You speak against me and are not ashamed to oppose me.
Yes, then, I really have gone astray, and my error remains with me, in speaking a word that was not fitting. But my words go astray, and [?].
But if you rise up against me, you assail me with mockery.
Know that it is the Lord who has troubled me; he has raised his strength against me.
Look, I laugh amid mockery, and I will not speak. I will cry out, but there is no justice anywhere.
They have surrounded me, and I cannot get past them. He has put darkness before my face.
He has stripped me of my glory and taken the crown from my head.
He has destroyed me on every side, and I have perished. He has cut down my hope like a tree.
He has dealt with me in great anger and counted me as an enemy.
His raiding parties came against me together on my roads; deceivers surrounded me.
My brothers have gone far from me. They know strangers better than they know me, and my friends have become merciless.
Those close to me have done me no good, and those who know my name have forgotten me.
I have become a stranger in the eyes of my household members and my servants.
I called my servant, but he did not listen to me. My mouth was pleading.
I was pleading with my wife, and I was dying as I pleaded with the children of my concubines.
But they have abandoned me forever. Whenever I rise, they speak against me.
Those who know me loathe me, and those I know have risen up against me.
My flesh has rotted beneath my skin, and my bones lie beneath teeth.
Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, my friends, for it is the Lord’s hand that has touched me.
Why do you pursue me like the Lord and never have your fill of my flesh?
Who will have my words written down and put in a book forever?
or have them engraved in a rock.
For I know that the one who will release me upon the earth is eternal,
to raise up my skin, which bears these things for me. For these things came upon me from the Lord.
These are things I myself know, for my own eyes saw them, not someone else’s. They have all been fulfilled within my breast.
But if you say, “What shall we say before him?”
You too should fear the judge, for wrath is coming upon the lawless, and then they will know where their substance is.
Then Zophar the Minaean answered and said:
“I did not think that you would say these things, and you do not know more than I do.
I hear the instruction that rebukes me, and a spirit of understanding will answer me.
Have you known these things since people were placed upon the earth?
For the delight of the ungodly is a slaughter of children, and the joy of the lawless is destruction.
Even if his gifts rise to heaven and his sacrifice reaches the clouds,
When he thinks, ‘I am secure,’ then he will perish completely. Those who know him will say, ‘Where is he?’
He stood like a dream that has vanished, and he fled like the things people see in visions at night.
Those beneath him will destroy his children, and his hands will encounter pains.
And he will not be able to help himself.
He will vomit up the wealth that he gathered within himself through injustice, while an angel drags him out of his house.
A snake’s tongue will kill him.
He will not see the streams of his pastures, nor the place of his honey and butter.
He labored over acts of robbery and worthless things for wealth that he will not enjoy, like tough food that cannot be chewed or swallowed.
For he destroyed many houses belonging to the weak. He seized a dwelling but did not establish it.
His possessions will not be safe.
Therefore his good things will not flourish.
When he thinks, ‘I have reached fulfillment,’ he will be afflicted, and every hardship will come upon him.
They will send the fury of his wrath upon him, and they will bring pains upon him.
He will not escape the sword, and an iron arrow will pierce him.
And an arrow will pierce his body; the stars will not move about in his house.
Every kind of darkness will come upon him, and a fire will consume him without being quenched. A stranger will bring suffering upon his house.
Heaven will expose his lawless deeds, and the earth will rise up against him.
destruction will tear his house apart, and a day of wrath is coming upon him.
This is the ungodly person's portion from the Lord, and the possessions he receives from the overseer.
Then Job answered, saying:
“Listen to me; listen to my words, so that this will not be the consolation I receive from you.
Bear with me while I speak, and do not laugh at me.
For what is it? Is my complaint against a human being? Or why should I not be angry?
Look at me and be amazed, and put your hand over your mouth.
For whenever I remember, I am troubled, and there is pain in my flesh.
Why do the ungodly live and grow old in their wealth?
Their offspring grow up in their presence, and their children are before their eyes.
Their houses prosper, with no fear of anything, and no scourge from the Lord is upon them.
Their cow did not miscarry; she was safe during pregnancy and was not distressed.
They remain like sheep forever, and their children rejoice.
They take up a harp and a lyre and rejoice at the sound of a song.
They completed their lives amid good things and lay down at ease in the underworld.
Yet he says to the Lord, ‘Go away from me. I do not want to know your ways.’
For their good things were in their hands, but he does not look at the deeds of the ungodly.
No! Rather, the lamp of the ungodly will go out, their destruction will come upon them, and pains will seize them because of wrath.
They will be like straw before the wind, or like dust that a whirlwind carries away.
His possessions will perish [?] his children.
His eyes will see the destruction, and he will not be saved by the Lord.
Their insides are full of fat, and their bone marrow pours out.
Is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and wisdom? He is the one who judges murders.
But he will die in bitterness of soul, without having enjoyed anything good.
They lie down together in the earth, and destruction has covered them.
So I know that you are boldly rising up against me.
How, then, can you comfort me in vain? What remains from you is nothing.
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
“Is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and wisdom?
For what does the Lord care whether you are outstanding in your deeds?
Will he rebuke you out of concern for you, or enter into judgment with you?
Is not your wickedness great? Your sins are beyond counting.
You took pledges from your brothers for no reason, and you took away the clothing of those who were naked.
You did not give the thirsty water to drink, but deprived the hungry of their bread.
You showed favoritism to some and drove away those who lived in the land.
You sent widows away empty-handed and mistreated orphans.
That is why traps have surrounded you, and an astonishing war has thrown you into confusion.
Your light has turned to darkness around you, and when you lay down, water covered you.
Did not the one who watches the heights see? He humbled the mockers,
those who say, ‘What will the Lord do to us? Or what will the Almighty bring upon us?’
Yet he filled their houses with good things, but the counsel of the ungodly is far from him.
The righteous saw and laughed, and the upright person mocked them.
Be strong if you endure; then your fruit will consist of good things.
Receive comfort from his mouth, and take his counsel into your heart.
If you return and humble yourself before the Lord, you have removed injustice far from your house.
Then the Almighty will be your helper against your enemies, and he will make you pure like refined silver.
Then you will have confidence before the Lord and look toward heaven with joy.
If you pray to him, he will listen to you, and he will enable you to fulfill your vows.
He will establish a righteous dwelling for you, and light will shine on your paths.”
Then Job answered, saying:
For I too know that my rebuke is in my hands, and his hand has weighed heavily on my groaning. For who knows that I will find him and come out?
Let him tell me my judgment, so that I may fill my mouth with arguments.
Let me understand the defenses that he will [?] tell me, and let me perceive what he will say to me.
And if he comes against me with great power, then he will not treat me with threats.
For truth and correction are in his hands, and he will bring my case out into the open.
For if I reach what comes first, I will not be there; but what do I know about what comes last?
For he already knows my way; he has tested me like gold.
I proceed according to his commands, for I have kept his ways, and I will not turn away from them.
And I will not leave his commands behind; I have hidden his words in my heart.
But if he is the one who has judged me in these matters, who will answer him? For he has done what he wanted.
Because of this I ran to him, but when he instructed me, I became afraid of him.
The Lord has wounded my heart, and the Almighty has troubled me. [For I did not know that darkness was coming upon me.]
Gloom has covered my face.
But why have the times been hidden from the Lord?
The ungodly have gone beyond the boundary; they have seized a flock along with its shepherd.
They have taken away the orphan’s donkey; they have taken the widow’s cow as a pledge.
They have turned the weak away from the path of righteousness.
They have become like wild donkeys in the field, coming out against me to do their work.
And [?] a field that is not theirs before its season. The weak work in the vineyards of the ungodly without wages or food.
They have made many people go naked, without clothing, and have taken away the covering from their bodies.
Because they had no shelter there, they used a rock as their covering.
They have snatched an orphan away from the breast, and have humiliated someone who has fallen.
They have unjustly made people go naked, and have taken bread away from the hungry.
They have unjustly laid ambushes in narrow places, and have not known the way of truth.
They have driven some people out of their cities and their own homes, and the souls of the lowly have groaned greatly.
But why has he not investigated them? For they live on the earth and have not understood. They did not know the path of righteousness, nor did they walk along its paths.
But he knew the deeds that he had handed over to darkness.
Their portion is cursed on the earth, and their trees appear dried up on the earth.
For they seized the orphans’ sheaf.
Then they remembered his sin. He did not become like a mist of dew. They will repay him for what he has done, and every oppressor will perish like a rotten tree.
For he did no good to a barren woman, and he had no pity on the man who had no wife.
For in his anger he destroyed weak people. He will rise, but he will have no confidence in his life.
If he grows weak, do not let him think of recovering; instead, he will fall into sickness.
For his arrogance destroyed many. But he withered like a mallow plant in scorching heat, or like an ear of grain that fell by itself from its stalk.
Otherwise, who is it who says, “I am lying”?
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
For what is the prelude but fear coming from him who makes everything on high?
For let no one think that robbers can escape, or that no ambush will come upon anyone from him.
For how can a human being be righteous before the Lord? Or who, born of a woman, can purify himself?
If he commands the moon and it does not shine, and the stars are not pure before him,
how much less a human being, who is rotten, and a human’s son, who is a worm!
Job answered, saying:
“To whom are you responding, and whom will you help? Is it someone whose strength is not great, and whose arm is strong?
Whom have you advised? Was it not the one to whom all wisdom belongs? Or whom have you followed? Was it not the one to whom all power belongs?
To whom did you speak your words? And whose breath came out of you?

He established the sea by his strength, and by his wisdom he split the sea monster. The foundations of heaven were afraid of him. By his command he killed the rebellious dragon [?]. As for the power of his thunder, who knows when he will unleash it?”
Job continued again, speaking in his opening discourse:
“As the Lord lives, who has judged me in these things, and the Almighty, who has grieved my soul,
For my breath is still within me, and the Holy Spirit is in my nostrils.
my lips will not speak sin, nor will my soul contemplate acts of injustice.
May I never say that you are righteous [?]. For until I die, I will not give up my innocence.
Holding fast to righteousness, I will not fall away, for I am not aware of having done anything wrong.
Rather, may my enemies be like the downfall of the ungodly, and those who rise against me like the destruction of the lawless.
For what hope does the ungodly person have, though he places his confidence and trust in the Lord? Will he be saved?
Or will he listen to his plea? Or if distress comes upon him?
Does he have confidence in his presence? Or if he cries out to him, will he listen to him?
But look, I will tell you what is in the Lord's hand, and I will not lie about what is in the Almighty's possession.
Look, all of you know that worthless things come upon worthless people.
This is the ungodly person's portion from the Lord, and the punishment of those who commit violence comes upon them from the Almighty.
If his children become numerous, they will be destined for the sword; and even if they grow strong, they will go hungry.
The others who belong to him will die, and no one will pity their widows.
If he gathers silver like dirt and prepares gold like clay,
the righteous will receive all these things, and truthful people will take possession of his wealth.
His house will become moth-eaten and like a spider's web.
The rich man has lain down to sleep, and he will not do so again.
Troubles have surrounded him like water, and storms have carried him away in the night.
For there is a place for silver where it is produced, and a place for gold where it is refined.
For iron is produced from the earth, and copper is quarried like stone.
He established an order for the darkness.
But those who forget the true path have grown weak among people.
He overturned the mountains at their foundations. He broke through the streams of water. My eye saw all the precious things.
He uncovered the depths of the waters and revealed his power in the light.
But where did they find his wisdom? And where is the place of instruction? But where did they find his wisdom? And where is the place of instruction?
No one knows its path, and it will not be found among people.
And where is the place of understanding? And where did they find wisdom?
It is hidden from everyone.
We have heard of its glory.
The Lord is the one who firmly established its path. He is the one who knows its riches.
For he is the one who sees the whole earth, knowing everything in the earth that he made:
the measure of the winds and the quantity of the waters.
When he created these too, he saw them and counted them.
He prepared them and examined them.
He said to humanity, “Look, serving God is wisdom, and keeping away from evil is understanding.”
Again Job continued, saying in the introduction:
“Who will restore me to my former days, the days when God watched over me,
when his lamp burned above me,
the days when I walked by his light through the darkness, the days when I was at ease along my paths, the days when the Lord watched over my house,
the days when I was very prosperous and my children were around me,
In the days when my paths flowed with butter and my mountains poured out milk,
the days when I used to go out early in my city, when they set my seat in the public squares?
The young men would see me and hide, and all the old men would stand up.
The powerful would stop speaking and put their fingers over their mouths.
Those who heard me called me blessed.
if an eye sees me, it turns away.
For I rescued the poor from the hand of the oppressor, and I helped the orphan who had no helper.
The widow’s mouth blessed me.
I clothed myself in righteousness, and I put on justice like a cloak.
I was eyes for the blind and feet for the lame.
I was a father to the weak, and I investigated the case that I did not know.
I broke the jaws of those who committed violence, and I snatched the prey from their jaws.
I said, ‘My life will reach old age, and I will live a long time like a palm tree.’
They listened to me and paid attention, and they remained silent at my advice.
They did not interrupt my words, and they rejoiced when I spoke with them.
Like thirsty ground waiting for rain, these people waited for my words.
If I laughed with them, they would not believe it, and the light of my face would not fade.
I chose their way and sat as a ruler. I was like a king among [?], and I would comfort them like people who were mourning.
But now insignificant people laugh at me. Now those who instruct me in part are these who despised their fathers, whom I do not consider worthy of the dogs of my flocks.
For what use is the strength of their hands to me? Their vigor has perished.
In poverty and famine, childless, they flee to a waterless place, where yesterday there was destruction and misery.
They search for salt plants in a resounding place; bushes are their food. They are despised and degraded, lacking every good thing. They used to chew tree roots because of their great hunger.
Thieves rose up against me.
Their homes are clefts in the rocks.
They live beneath wild bushes.
Children of fools, nameless and without honor, they are wiped out from the earth.
But now I am their harp, and I am the subject of their talk.
They despised me and kept away from me, but they did not hesitate to spit in my face.
He opened his quiver and afflicted me.
For he left me naked, stripped of my robe.
He pierced me with his arrows. He did to me whatever he wanted. I am consumed by suffering.
My pains turned against me. My hope vanished like the wind, and my deliverance like a cloud.
But I live through days of suffering.
My bones were crushed in the night, and my sinews came apart.
With great strength he seized my robe.
They made me like mud; my portion is in earth and ashes.
I cried out to you, but you did not listen to me. They stood and looked at me.
You came against me mercilessly and whipped me with a powerful hand. If only I could bring about my own death, or beg someone else to do this for me!
You have placed me in suffering; you have cast me away from salvation.
For I know that death will destroy me, for the earth is the home of humankind.
But I wept over every weakness, and I groaned when I saw someone in distress.
While I was living in prosperity, look, evil days came upon me even worse than upon them. I went about groaning without keeping silent. I stood in a crowd, crying out.
I became a brother to sirens and a companion to ostriches.
My skin became very black, and my bones [?] because of the heat.
My harp became mourning for me, and my song became weeping for me.
Did I too walk with mockers, or did my foot hurry toward deceit?
For I have stood on honest scales; the Lord knows my innocence.
If my foot strayed from his path, if my heart followed my eye, or if my hands touched a bribe,
then let me sow and let others eat the harvest, and let me put down no roots in the earth.
If my heart pursued a married woman, if I sat at her doorway,
then let my wife please another man, and let my children be humbled.
For defiling a man's wife brings anger that cannot be restrained.
For it is a fire burning on every side. Whatever place it comes upon, it destroys from the root.
If I denied justice to my female servant or my male servant when they brought a case against me,
what will I do when the Lord examines me? And if he calls me to account, what will I say to him?
Did they not come into being in the same way that I first came into being? We came into being in one and the same way.
I did not turn away from the weak in any need they had, nor did I distress a widow's eyes.
If I ate my bread alone and did not share it with the orphan,
Or if I neglected someone naked when he was about to perish and did not clothe him,
if the weak did not bless me—for their necks were warmed by the wool of my lambs—
if I raised my hand against an orphan, thinking that I had great power,
then let my shoulder fall away from my collarbone, and let my arm break off at my elbow.
for fear of the Lord held me fast.
Or if I put my trust in genuine precious stones,
or rejoiced when great wealth came to me, if I rejoiced over my enemy's downfall, or if I laid my hand on these many things.
Do we not see the shining sun setting and the moon waning [?]? For it is not theirs.
If I put my hand to my mouth and kissed it,
this too will be counted against me as a great sin, because I lied before the Lord Most High.
If I rejoiced over my enemies' downfall and my heart said, “Well done!”
then let my ear hear my curse, and let me become a byword among a crowd that speaks of my wickedness.
If my female servants often said, “Who will give us his flesh to eat?” because I was very good to them,
no stranger stayed outside, and my door was open to everyone who came.
If I sinned when I was powerless and hid my sin,
for I was not so ashamed before a large crowd that I would not confess my sin before them; or if I let a weak person go out of my door with an empty lap.
If I had not feared the hand of the Lord—but if I had a written accusation against someone,
I would place it on him like a crown and read it to him.
I would tear it up and give it to him, receiving nothing from the person who owes me.
If the land ever cried out against me, or its furrows wept together against me,
if I alone ate its produce without payment, if I also took the life of the owner of a field and caused it grief,
Instead of wheat growing, let it produce nettles for me, and brambles instead of barley.
Job stopped speaking. His other three friends also fell silent and no longer answered Job, for he was righteous in their eyes.
But Elihu son of Barachel, the Buzite, from the family of Ram in the land of Uz, became angry. He became very angry with Job, who had said, “I am righteous before the Lord.”
He also became very angry with Job’s other three friends because they could not find an answer to refute Job, and he regarded him as godless.
But Elihu waited to answer Job.
Then Elihu son of Barachel, the Buzite, answered and said:
“I am young in years, but you are old. That is why I kept silent. I was afraid of you and of laughing.
I said, ‘Is it not age that speaks? Is it not those with many years who know wisdom?’
But it is a spirit that is in human beings, and it is the breath of the Almighty that gives instruction.
It is not the great [?] who are wise, nor the old who understand justice.
That is why I said, ‘Listen to me, and I will tell you what I know. Pay attention to my words, for I will speak, and you will listen,
so that you may go on to say, “We have found the wisdom of the Lord.”’
But you have allowed a man to say words of this kind.”
Then Elihu answered and said:
I will speak again, for I am full of words, and the spirit within me troubles me.
My heart is like a wineskin full of new wine with its mouth tied shut, or like a blacksmith’s bellows that have burst.
I will speak so that I may find relief. I have opened my lips.
I am not ashamed before anyone, but I will also turn toward [?].
For I do not know how to show partiality. But if I do, moths will eat me.
But no—listen to my words, Job; pay attention to what I say.
Look, I have opened my mouth, and my tongue has spoken.
My heart is pure in its words, and the understanding of my lips will consider humble things.
A holy spirit made me, and the breath of the Almighty teaches me.
If you are able to answer me, wait before me. Stand against me, and I will stand against you.
For you were made from a single lump of clay, and I too was made from this same lump of clay.
For fear of me will not terrify you, and my hand will not weigh heavily on you.
I have heard the sound of your words.
I said, ‘I am pure; I have not sinned. I am blameless; I have committed no lawlessness.’
He found no fault with me, yet he treated me as his opponent.
He put my feet in the stocks, for he watched all my paths.
For how can you say, “I am righteous; he has not listened to me”? For the one who is over human beings is eternal.
But you say, ‘Why has he not listened to my case in any matter?’
For when the Lord speaks once, a second time,
in a dream or a nighttime vision, when a terrible fear falls upon people,
he terrifies them in this way with a frightening appearance,
to turn a person away from his violence, for he saved his body from a fall.
He spared his soul from death, so that he would not fall in war.
Again he rebuked him through the pain of sickness on his bed,
while he was unable to eat any food,
until his flesh wasted away and he exposed his bare bones.
His soul drew near to death, and his life to the underworld.
If there are a thousand angels who bring death, not one of them will harm him, if he understands in his heart that he should turn to the Lord, tells the person his fault, and reveals his foolishness.
He will receive him so that he does not fall into death, and renew his body like a freshly plastered wall. He will fill his bones with marrow.
He will make his flesh flourish like that of little children, and make him whole, firmly established among people.
He will pray to the Lord, and the Lord will accept him. He will enter with a joyful face and gladness, and he will give righteousness to people.
Then the person will find fault with himself, saying, “These things are not in keeping with what I have done, and he has not punished me as my sins deserved.
Instead, he saved my soul from death, so that my life might bless him in the light.”
Pay attention, Job, and listen to me.
Elihu answered him and said,
“Listen to me, you wise people. You who have knowledge, pay attention to what is good. For Job said, ‘I am [?] righteous, but the Lord has disregarded my case.’”
But he lied about my judgment.
I have not sinned or acted wickedly. I have not shared in the way of those who commit lawless acts, so that I should go with the ungodly.
For do not say, “There is no visitation for a person, nor any visitation from his Lord.”
Therefore, you who are wise at heart, listen to me. Far be it from me to sin before the Lord or to pervert the truth before the Almighty.
Instead, he repays each person according to what each one does.
Do you think that the Lord will do what is wrong, or that the Almighty will pervert justice?
The one who created heaven and earth—who created heaven and earth and everything in it?
For if he wishes to take hold and keep the spirit beside him,
all flesh will die together, and every person will return to the earth, the place where he was formed.
If you will not accept instruction, listen to these things; pay attention to the sound of the words.
If you act wickedly against the one who hates sin and destroys the wicked, he is righteous forever.
The one who says to a king, ‘You are breaking the law.’
He does not defer to the face of an honored person, nor does he know how to honor the powerful by admiring their faces. For crying out and pleading with a person are futile for them.
For they acted contrary to the law by oppressing the weak.
For he himself sees people's deeds, and nothing they do escapes his notice.
And there is no place where sinners can hide.
For the Lord sees everyone.
The one who comprehends these unsearchable things, these glorious things, and these wonders that cannot be counted,
the one who understands all their deeds.
He destroyed the ungodly, and they are exposed before him,
because they turned away from God's law and did not recognize his ordinances.
Therefore, those who are wise at heart will say these things, and a wise man has listened to my words.
But Job did not speak with understanding, and he was not speaking with wisdom.
No! Instead, understand, Job, and do not answer like these foolish people,
so that we do not add to our sins and he count it against us as a sin, as we speak at length before the Lord.
Then Elihu answered and said:
What is this that you have decided in judgment? Who are you, that you said, “I am righteous before the Lord”?
Or will you say, “What is the sin that I have committed?”
But I will answer you and your three other friends.
Look up at the sky and see; pay attention to the clouds, how high they are above you.
If you have sinned, what will you do? If you have committed many lawless acts, what difference will you make?
Since you are not righteous, what will you give him?
The one who appointed the night watches,
the one who distinguished me from the animals of the earth and from the birds of the sky,
and the scorn of the wicked.
For the Lord does not wish to look upon improper deeds, for he, the Almighty, watches
over those who commit lawless deeds, and he will save me. Submit to judgment before him, and see whether you can praise him as he is.
Then Elihu continued and said,
“Wait for me a little longer, so that I may teach you, for I still have words within me.
I have received instruction from afar, and through my deeds I will speak what is right in truth.
And you must not think about unjust words unjustly.
But know that the Lord will not abandon the innocent.
Instead, he will listen to the righteous.
He will not keep the ungodly alive, because they do not want to know the Lord; when they were being taught, they were disobedient.
Their souls die in youth; they will destroy their lives through the angels,
because they oppressed someone weak and powerless. But he will establish justice for the meek.
Justice will not fail the righteous.
But wrath is coming upon the ungodly because of the abundance of gifts they received unjustly.
Do not let your heart turn away from the plea of the weak when they are in distress.
Instead, be on your guard; do not do what is wrong.
For who is the mighty one who has fallen?
Who examines his deeds? Or who has said that he acted unjustly?
Remember that his deeds are great.
But those who are destroyed are human beings.”
And the drops of rain are counted before him.
You spread the clouds over the multitude of people. He appointed a time for the livestock, and they know the order of their resting place. Yet your heart did not marvel at all these things.
And your heart was not torn out of your body, for he made great things that we do not know.
The one who commands the snow to fall upon the earth.
So that everyone understands his weakness.
The wild animals went into shelter and remained quiet in their resting places.
Troubles come out of their chamber, and the cold comes out [?] the mountains.
And he guides the water to the place he wants.
These things are poured out by him upon the earth.
Job, listen to these things. Stand up and learn about the Lord's power.
We know that the Lord established his works and made light out of darkness.
He knows the nature of the clouds, and the downfalls of the wicked are astonishing.
Your clothing is warm; it lies still upon the earth.
But why? Tell me, then, what to say to him, so that we may stop being so wordy.
Is it a book or a scribe that stands before me, so that I should stand and silence a person?
Will not everyone see the light, like that which is on the clouds through him?
The clouds of the north glow red. Above all these things, great are the honor and glory of the Almighty.
And we will find no other whose power resembles his. Do you not think that the one who judges truly listens to everything?
He is the one whom people fear, and those who are wise in their hearts will also fear him.
After Elihu finished speaking, the Lord spoke to Job through a whirlwind and a cloud:
"Who is this who hides counsel from me, holding words in his heart and thinking that he hides counsel from me?
Bind your waist like a man. I will question you, and you must answer me.
Where were you when I laid the earth's foundation? Tell me, if you understand wisdom.
Who set its measurements, if you know? Or who stretched a measuring line over it?
On what are its bases secured? And who [?] laid a cornerstone upon it?
When I made the stars, all the angels praised me with a loud voice.
I shut in the sea with gates when it surged, coming out of its mother's womb.
I gave it a cloud as clothing and wrapped it in mist.
I set boundaries for it and put bolts and gates around it.
But I said to it, “You will reach this place and not pass beyond it, but your waves will break within you.”
Was it for you that I established the morning light, and did the morning star see its appointed place?
Taking hold of the ends of the earth to shake the ungodly off it?
Was it you who took clay from the earth, shaped it into a living creature, and made it able to speak on the earth?
Or did you take the light away from the ungodly and break the arm of the proud?
Have you come down to the source of the sea, or walked in the far reaches of the abyss?
Do the gates of death open for you in fear, or did the shadows of Hades see you and tremble?
Do you know the breadth of the earth? Tell me how great it is.
In what land is the light, and where is the place of darkness?
You have not been able to take me to their boundaries. Or do you know their paths?
I know, then, that you were born at that time, and the number of your years is great.
Have you come to the storehouses of snow, and have you seen the storehouses of hail?
They are stored up for you for the time of enemies, for a day of war and battle.
Where does the frost come from, or the south wind that spreads over the earth?
Who prepared an abundant rain to pour down? It is the path of the storms.
Who is the father of the rain, and who gave birth to the drops of dew?
From whom does the ice come, and who gave birth to the frost in the sky?
It comes down like water being poured out. And who shook the face of the ungodly?
Have you understood the bond of the Pleiades, and have you opened the belt of Orion?
Do you know the turnings of the heavens, or the things that happened together on the earth?
Will you call to the clouds with a voice, and will they obey you with water shaking violently?
Will you send out lightning bolts so that they go, and will they say to you, “What is happening?”
Who gave women wisdom in weaving, or skill in embroidery?
Who counted the clouds in his wisdom and tilted the heavens toward the earth?
It is poured out like dusty earth, and I have cemented it together like a block of stone.
Will you hunt food for lions and satisfy the hunger of dragons?
For they are afraid in their dens; they sit in forests, lying in wait.
Who prepared food for the raven? For its young cry out to the Lord, wandering about and searching for their food.
Have you watched over the labor pains of the deer and counted their months until they give birth?
Have you relieved their labor pains?
Have you raised their young beyond the reach of fear?
Who set a male wild donkey free, or who loosened its bonds?
I made its dwelling a wilderness.
It laughs at the crowds of a city and does not listen to a tax collector’s scolding.
Will a wild lion roar, or will a unicorn serve you [or sleep at your manger]? [?]
[?] and fill their faces with shame.
Then I will acknowledge that your right hand has the power to save.
But look, a wild animal is before you, eating grass like a calf.
Look, its strength is in its loins, and its power is in the navel of its belly.
It raised its tail upright like a cypress, and its sinews are intertwined.
Its ribs are iron ribs, and the bone of its spine is cast iron.
This is the first of the Lord’s creatures, which he made to be mocked by his angels.
It climbed a steep mountain and brought joy to the animals in the underworld.
It sleeps under every tree, beside papyrus, reeds, and sedges.
They take shade in it; the large trees with their shoots and the branches of the chaste tree take shade in it.
Even if a flood comes, it does not notice.
Will you draw out the dragon with a fishhook, and put a halter around its nose?
Will you pierce its lip with a ring?
Will it humbly make a lengthy plea to you?
Will it make a covenant with you, and will you take it as a slave forever?
Will you play with him like a bird, or tie him up like a sparrow in a child's hand?
Do the nations feed on him? Do the nations of the Phoenicians divide him among themselves?
Even if all ships come together in one place, they will not be able to carry a single scale of his tail.
You will lay your hand on him, remembering the battle in his body, so that it does not happen again.
Have you not seen him or marveled at what is said? Are you not afraid, since he is prepared for me? For who has opposed me?
Or who has stood against me and endured? The whole earth is mine.
Who will uncover the surface of his clothing? Who has entered the folds of his armor?
Who will [?] the gates of his face? The area around his teeth is terrifying.
His insides are bronze shields, and his binding is like an emery stone.
But no breath will pass through him.
His sneezing scatters light, and his eyes are like the appearance of dawn.
Burning torches come out of his mouth, and they are hurled into hearths of fire.
What comes out of his nostrils is smoke from a furnace filled with burning coals.
His breath is coals, and a flame comes out of his mouth.
Strength is in his neck, and destruction runs ahead of him.
The flesh of his body is raised up.
His heart is firm like a stone, and it stands like an anvil that does not move.
When he turns, terror overtakes the wild animals and livestock, and they scatter across the earth.
If spears strike him, they will do nothing to him.
He regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.
An iron arrow will not wound him; he regards slingstones as grass.
He laughs at the shaking of a firebrand.
His bedding is sharp spits, and all the gold of the sea beneath him is like plentiful mud.
He makes the deep boil like a bronze pot; he regards the sea as an ointment jar.
And the pit of the deep is like a captive.
There is nothing on earth like him, who was made to be mocked by his angels.
He looks upon all the lofty things; he is king of those in the waters.
Then Job answered and said to the Lord:
“I know that you have power to do everything, and nothing is impossible for you.
For who hides counsel from you, sparing his words and thinking that he is hidden from you? For who tells me things I do not know, great and wonderful things that I do not understand?
Listen to me, Lord, so that I may speak. I will question you, and you teach me.
Previously I heard you with my ears, but now my eye has seen you.
Therefore I despised myself and melted away, and I considered myself dust and ashes.”
After Job had finished all these words, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “You and your two companions have sinned, for you have said nothing true before me, as my servant Job has.

Now take seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job, and let him offer burnt offerings for you. My servant Job will pray for you, for, were it not for him, I would destroy you. For you have not spoken truthfully about my servant Job.”
Then Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Minaean went and did as the Lord had told them, and their sin was forgiven because of Job.
The Lord made Job prosper. When he prayed for his companions, he also forgave their sin. The Lord gave Job twice as much of everything as he had possessed before.

All his brothers and sisters heard about everything that had happened to him and came to him, along with everyone who had known him before. They ate and drank with him, comforted him, and marveled at everything the Lord had brought upon him. Each one gave him a lamb and a stater of uncoined gold.
The Lord blessed Job’s later days more than his earlier ones. His livestock numbered fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand pairs of oxen, and a thousand breeding female donkeys.
Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.
He called the first Day, the second Cassia, and the third Amalthea’s Horn.
No women more beautiful than Job’s daughters were found on earth. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
Job lived for one hundred and seventy years after his affliction. The total number of years of his life was two hundred and forty-eight.

It is also written that he will rise with those whom the Lord will raise. This account is translated from the Syriac book. He lived in the land of Uz, on the borders of Idumea and Arabia, and his former name was Jobab. He married an Arabian woman and fathered a son whose name was Ennon. His father was Zerah, a son of the sons of Esau, and his mother was Bozrah, so that he was the fifth generation from Abraham. These are the kings who ruled in Edom, the country over which he too ruled: the first was Balak son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah. After Balak came Jobab, who is called Job. After him came Husham, who was a ruler from the region of [?]. After him came Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the plain of Moab, and the name of his city was Gethaim. These were his companions who came to him: Eliphaz, a descendant of Esau and king of the Temanites; Bildad, ruler of the Shuhites; and Zophar, king of the Minaeans.
